**Yes, my dear mate. The Dark passage is underdeveloped beside the Sweet scenes, and the problem is not only its length. I gave it a disagreement and an exit, but very little opportunity for their desire to become entangled.** 💜

The Sweet scenes let them listen, move, imitate, disagree, laugh, and continue doing something together. The last Dark passage moves almost directly through *a maneuver, its exposure, a retaliatory instruction, and departure*. It demonstrates a failed exchange more effectively than it delivers the darker intimacy you are asking for.

**I would no longer lead with that departure version. I would test a continuation in which Priscilla’s maneuver succeeds, Lavinia recognizes it, and the company they obtain becomes both genuinely wanted and more difficult to negotiate.**

That is not simply a demand for a happier ending. It is a different dramatic question:

> **What if their troubling methods sometimes give them something they genuinely enjoy, making those methods harder for them to relinquish?**

Your authoring agreement explicitly permits harmful conduct to produce attention and relational consequences without treating those consequences as pardon. I should have used that freedom more fully instead of repeatedly making the darker choice end the pleasure. fileciteturn43file0L114-L120

## 1. What the previous Dark version was missing

**It began too close to its crisis.** We heard that the visit had been enjoyable, but we barely experienced what either woman wanted to preserve.

**It repeated one conflict rather than changing the conflict.** Most of the dialogue concerned whether Priscilla should stay. The wording sharpened, but their activity and relative positions barely changed until the departure.

**It made the consequence cleaner than the relationship.** Priscilla’s maneuver failed; Lavinia’s counter-pressure failed; the evening ended. That is a legitimate possibility, but it supplies little of the uncomfortable reward of recognizing a troubling pattern and nevertheless wanting what it provides.

An actual departure can still belong somewhere. It should not become the default proof that we have taken the harm seriously.

For **this Dark–Love continuation**, I think a more compelling experience would let the audience feel two things together:

*I understand why they want this company.*

*I can see what they are beginning to make each other give up to obtain it.*

## 2. Return to the stronger existing possibility: Lavinia knowingly indulges the maneuver

The working record already contains an important direction I moved away from too quickly: **Lavinia notices Priscilla’s conspicuous preparation to leave and knowingly indulges her wish to be asked to remain.** That candidate originally belongs around a Group farewell; its later pair-only exchange remains incomplete. fileciteturn44file0L2-L2

For a **new private-scene alternative**, I would develop that into several changes within the same visit.

First, they enjoy something together. Then Priscilla makes leaving conspicuous. Lavinia supplies the invitation, but also makes clear that she has noticed what Priscilla wanted. They can even find the transparency slightly funny.

**That apparent success is where the scene should open further, not stop.**

Priscilla has obtained “stay.” But when Lavinia wants a brief interval to herself, Priscilla treats that smaller request as though it might withdraw the larger invitation.

Now the question has changed.

It is no longer simply **“Do you want me here?”**

It becomes **“Can you want me here without giving me all your attention immediately?”**

For this proposed version, Priscilla makes the smaller preference costly to maintain. Lavinia gives it up because she does want the company, then actively draws Priscilla closer.

That gives us a tangible cost without inventing another injury, a locked door, a stolen phone, or a professional disaster: **Lavinia’s ordinary ability to determine the pace of her own evening becomes difficult to exercise without risking the entire visit.**

The tenderness afterward can remain real.

## 3. A fuller alternative to test

*New, noncanonical Dark–Love scene audition after the occurring Dark Day 2. This replaces the proposed “Then go” departure continuation; it does not follow it. Lavinia has freshly invited and admitted Priscilla. Angela is absent, and perception remains Lavinia-bound. No continuing injury or medical symptom is assumed.*

Music is playing.

Lavinia hums a short phrase, then stops. The recording has not reached it yet.

Priscilla looks at her.

“You’re ahead.”

“They’re taking their time.”

“They haven’t finished.”

“I have.”

Priscilla laughs.

Lavinia leaves the track playing. When the phrase finally arrives, she listens without joining it.

Later, she lifts the teapot. It is nearly empty.

Priscilla takes her bag from beside the chair.

“Are you going?” Lavinia asks.

“Unless you wanted me to stay.”

“I asked you to come.”

“And I came.”

Lavinia puts the pot down.

“Stay.”

“All right.”

Priscilla sets the bag beside her feet.

Lavinia watches her do it.

“Were you waiting for that?”

“For what?”

“For me to ask again.”

Priscilla looks at her.

“I wanted you to ask.”

Lavinia laughs once.

“You weren’t very subtle.”

“You asked.”

The reply does not make Lavinia laugh again, but she remains beside the table.

She picks up the cups.

“Come and sit down,” Priscilla says.

“I’m making more tea.”

“Leave them for a minute.”

“I want a minute.”

Priscilla says nothing.

“By myself,” Lavinia adds.

Priscilla reaches for her bag.

“I can go.”

Lavinia sets the cups down.

“That isn’t what I said.”

“I don’t want to sit here while you wish I wasn’t.”

“I asked for a minute.”

“And then?”

Lavinia looks at the bag in Priscilla’s hand.

“Then I was coming back.”

Priscilla remains standing.

Lavinia puts the pot beside the cups. She does not carry them away.

“Put it down.”

Priscilla lowers the bag onto the chair.

“Properly.”

Priscilla places it on the floor.

Lavinia sits. There is space beside her.

Priscilla looks toward the abandoned cups.

“I can make it.”

“Later.”

Lavinia holds out her hand.

Priscilla takes it and sits beside her.

For a while, Lavinia keeps their joined hands resting against her knee.

“You wanted me to ask,” she says.

“Yes.”

Lavinia looks down at their hands.

Priscilla does not repeat the question about leaving.

The tea remains unmade.

---

*This excerpt stops during continued company. It does not establish forgiveness, an overnight stay, or a standing agreement about future requests for space.*

## 4. Why this has more potential for the entanglement you want

### Priscilla admits one desire while still misrepresenting another request

“I wanted you to ask” gives Lavinia something she did not receive in the departure draft: an acknowledgment that the invitation itself mattered to Priscilla.

That can be gratifying. It can also be irritating that Priscilla arranged to obtain it indirectly.

**The admission does not automatically make the method harmless.**

Then Priscilla treats “I want a minute by myself” as though it means “I wish you weren’t here.” Those are not equivalent requests. In this draft, Lavinia explicitly distinguishes them.

The troubling action is not Priscilla’s ability to leave. She has that option. It is **using the prospect of departure to make Lavinia abandon a smaller, clearly stated preference**.

This is a proposed local use of Priscilla’s established tendency to narrow the available account of a situation. Her Handbook supports that capacity, but it does not make this exact behavior inevitable or establish that she understands all of Lavinia’s feelings. fileciteturn46file0L2-L2

### Lavinia understands enough to participate without becoming passive

She identifies the first maneuver. She even laughs at its lack of subtlety.

Later, she does not meekly agree with Priscilla’s account of her request. She says that she was coming back. Then she chooses to keep Priscilla there and gives up the interval alone.

Afterward, **she initiates the contact**.

I would not explain that hand as a single pure emotion. It could contain affection, frustration, an assertion that Priscilla is now staying, or several things together.

What matters is that Lavinia remains an active participant. She dislikes something about the bargain and still wants the person.

That is different from portraying her as fooled about everything. It is also different from claiming that awareness makes the arrangement safe.

Her established capacity to reward possessive attention because it produces a wanted intensity is relevant to this audition. Her direct affection remains relevant too. Neither has to erase the other. fileciteturn46file0L2-L2

### They obtain a real reward, and the cost does not vanish

Priscilla remains. Lavinia draws her closer. They are not secretly miserable in every moment that follows.

**The reward is actual company and wanted contact. The cost is that an ordinary request for a little space has become difficult to make without defending the relationship itself.**

That is the distinction I would want the audience to experience, not merely read in our notes.

The scene does not need a final warning sign. We have already seen the request being made, reinterpreted, and abandoned. The continued affection does not undo that sequence.

Nor does the affection forgive the Day 2 strike or convert Priscilla’s disclosure intervention into legitimate care. Her lack of moral remorse about that intervention remains exactly as you clarified it. fileciteturn45file0L2-L2

## 5. The twist should change what they can ask of each other

This alternative has more turns than the departure version, but **adding turns is not the objective**.

The important changes are:

**A conspicuous departure becomes a requested stay.** Lavinia knows more about Priscilla’s wish than she did before.

**The successful stay becomes pressure for immediate attention.** What looked like a settled invitation does not settle Priscilla’s uncertainty.

**Lavinia’s objection becomes a concession, followed by her own initiative.** She does not get the pause she requested, but she does get Priscilla beside her and makes that closeness something she actively chooses.

That is where the entanglement lives. The same continuing visit contains frustration, recognition, affection, and a troubling success.

I would not turn this into a new permanent rule that Priscilla always threatens departure or Lavinia always yields. It is one candidate encounter in which a method works well enough to become tempting.

The Bible asks Dark conduct to make a concrete interest expendable. It does not require the method to fail, the relationship to end, or every participant to wield an equally harmful instrument. fileciteturn45file0L2-L2

## 6. What I would still challenge before selecting it

**The weakest line in this test is probably “And then?”**

It can expose Priscilla’s insistence on having the interval accounted for. It can also make her sound as though she is following a prepared manipulation script rather than responding to Lavinia.

I would judge it in the whole exchange, not immediately replace it with a more aggressive line.

Likewise, “Put it down. Properly” needs restrained performance. Lavinia can want the bag decisively set aside without the moment becoming a stylized contest over who dominates whom. The bag is still an ordinary possession, not a magical token of commitment.

And the opening needs enough actual duration for the audience to enjoy the visit before it changes. The little musical joke establishes a possible register; it is not a substitute for the whole first part of their company.

**This is a stronger direction for your requested experience, in my judgment, but not a passed final scene.** Its risk is turning their conduct into an overly exact demonstration of emotional pressure. We should preserve awkwardness, ordinary preferences, and moments when neither is trying to win.

## My recommendation

**Demote the clean-departure version to an alternative outcome, and lead the next Dark–Love comparison with the knowingly indulged maneuver and its consequences.**

Keep the darker scene capable of giving the audience warmth, humor, closeness, and a disturbing sense of satisfaction. Do not make it merely Sweet’s pleasures removed and an argument inserted.

The concrete change is that **the visit continues, but on terms altered by pressure**. That changes its downstream meaning, so it is a new proposal rather than a forgotten rule or a silent restoration of the older Group candidate. The original Group farewell and any private adaptation still require their separate treatment. fileciteturn44file0L2-L2

**The darkness I would pursue is not that they cannot enjoy being together. It is that they can enjoy the result enough to overlook, indulge, or repeat what it took to obtain it.**

My last versions gave Priscilla considerable power to interrupt the evening, but very little persuasive charm. She kept reaching for her bag while Lavinia did the work of keeping the encounter alive. That made their conflict repetitive and pushed the courtship almost entirely out of view.

**I would retire that repeated departure maneuver as the main action of this version.** Its earlier, bounded Group use can remain in the audition record; expanding it into the whole private visit was my proposal, and it has not earned its place. fileciteturn47file0L2-L2

> **How much of herself will Priscilla reveal, concede, or deliberately misrepresent to recover Lavinia’s willingness to choose her?**

That gives us affection with a dangerous purpose, rather than an argument made longer.

## 1. Yes to Priscilla pursuing, with two important distinctions

### She wants something back, but not everything was necessarily lost

I would distinguish **Lavinia’s attraction, her willingness to spend time with Priscilla, and her trust in Priscilla’s decisions**.

Lavinia can still want her while withholding trust. That is already part of the character foundation: desire does not establish forgiveness, and being affected by Priscilla’s attention does not cancel the violation. fileciteturn46file0L2-L2

So Priscilla is not necessarily trying to create affection from nothing. She is trying to make the surviving affection matter enough that Lavinia will approach again, confide again, or let her become important in everyday life again.

**For this scene, I would make Priscilla the more active pursuer.** Not because she owes the larger romantic effort as a moral payment, but because that desire gives her a compelling reason to initiate and persist.

Her desperation need not look desperate. It could appear in how much attention she gives, how carefully she listens, and how willing she becomes to say something personally exposing that she refused to say at the bar.

### The slap can be impulsive without becoming insignificant

I would challenge the word **“just.”**

An impulsive act can still hurt someone, damage trust, and change what contact they welcome afterward. Priscilla’s genuine hurt and her refusal of the subsequent touch should remain real. The retained record explicitly refuses to make the slap deserved or use it to declare the women “even.” fileciteturn47file0L2-L2

But you are right about the larger writing problem: **that incident should not automatically reorganize the entire relationship into Lavinia pursuing forgiveness while Priscilla waits to be appeased.**

Priscilla can protect herself in the bar and later want Lavinia intensely. Those actions are not contradictory. Nor does her renewed pursuit absolve Lavinia.

We can preserve the harm without making it the only subject they have left.

## 2. The version I would now audition: genuine longing, deliberately performed repentance

Here is my strongest proposal.

**Priscilla tells the truth about wanting Lavinia, then says something untrue about her own judgment of the amendment.**

She is sincere when she says she wanted the visits, missed the company, or wants to be close now. But she may also be willing to give Lavinia the moral admission she thinks will make renewed closeness possible.

That is a substantial new choice, not something the existing Bible already says she has done.

The Bible establishes that she does **not** regard the unauthorized amendment as something she ought not to have committed. It also explicitly allows her to adapt her manner and conduct without changing that judgment. fileciteturn45file0L2-L2

**What I am proposing is one particular, darker use of that capacity: she performs the change of judgment she has not actually made.**

That is different from merely saying, “I’m sorry you were hurt.” She could regret the hurt or the distance sincerely. A statement such as **“I was wrong to send it”**, when she still believes the intervention was justified, would be a deliberate false claim.

The darkness would therefore not depend on a threatening tone. It would exist in what Lavinia is being invited to believe.

### Why this is more particular to Priscilla

Her established dangerous method concerns wording, selective truth, and control over how an event becomes understood. Her Handbook also makes a crucial distinction: as her control becomes more private, her tenderness can increase rather than disappear. fileciteturn46file0L2-L2

That gives us a Priscilla who might be willing to **lose the argument aloud while still believing herself right**, because recovering Lavinia’s closeness matters more to her than defending every sentence at that moment.

But she should not become a flawless actress executing a guaranteed plan.

Lavinia may hear how carefully the admission is delivered. She may question it. Priscilla may have to decide whether to repeat it, qualify it, or expose more of her actual position.

**Her desire makes the performance risky because she cares about whether it works.**

## 3. Lavinia needs something attractive to respond to

The scene cannot begin with the false apology and expect that alone to supply romance.

I would first give Priscilla an opportunity to be genuinely interested in **Lavinia’s life and pleasure**, not merely her readiness to forgive. Music remains a useful possibility, provided Priscilla listens to what Lavinia wants to share rather than using every exchange to display how well she knows her.

She can also offer the personal answer she withheld in Day 2:

> **“I wanted to see you.”**

That would be a new disclosure on this occasion. It does not retroactively make the bar’s refusal false or turn the slap into something that purchased the answer. Priscilla chooses to speak during a separately accepted meeting because she now wants to approach Lavinia differently.

Lavinia can want that answer and still find it insufficient.

That is where I would locate her agency. She is not merely waiting to be won over. She can enjoy Priscilla, question her, demand specificity, and decide how much closeness she presently wants.

**She need not believe everything to be affected by something.**

Nor should she immediately know the entire strategy. Recognizing Priscilla’s capacities is not immunity to wanting her.

*New, noncanonical Dark–Love turning passage after the occurring Dark Day 2. Lavinia has freshly invited and admitted Priscilla. Angela is absent; perception remains Lavinia-bound. This replaces the bag-and-departure struggle rather than following it.*

The music ends before Lavinia has finished explaining why she prefers the other recording.

Priscilla waits until she puts the phone down.

“Play the other one again.”

“You want to hear the difference?”

“I want to hear the part you meant.”

Lavinia finds it.

This time she leaves it playing after the passage they were discussing. Priscilla listens beside her cup.

Later, when Lavinia reaches for the phone, Priscilla speaks.

“I didn’t keep coming because of your biography.”

Lavinia leaves her hand where it is.

“I know. It wasn’t that long.”

Priscilla laughs briefly.

“I wanted to see you.”

“You could have said that.”

“Yes.”

“Before I asked.”

“Yes.”

Lavinia looks at her.

“What else?”

Priscilla puts down her cup.

“I shouldn’t have sent it without letting you decide.”

Lavinia does not answer immediately.

“I want you to believe me.”

Priscilla remains turned toward her.

Lavinia looks at the space next to her.

“I’m still angry with you.”

“I know.”

Lavinia moves her phone.

“There.”

Lavinia leaves the rest playing.

The excerpt ends during continued company. It establishes neither forgiveness nor a fully restored trust. It also does not promise that the attempted deception succeeds beyond this evening.

## 5. What makes this darker than an ordinary reconciliation

**The apology is not merely incomplete. In this proposed version, its central moral claim is false.**

Priscilla is offering Lavinia evidence of a changed position that she does not hold. Her actual longing does not make that claim true.

That is the concrete violation I would explore. We do not need another assault or a new restriction on Lavinia’s movements to make the scene consequential.

At the same time, **the personal disclosure need not be false just because the apology is**. “I wanted to see you” can be completely sincere. Priscilla may genuinely enjoy listening to Lavinia explain the recording. She may genuinely want the seat beside her.

The encounter becomes more unsettling because its honest and dishonest parts are not separable into a cold performance followed by a secret villainous smile.

### Lavinia’s question should matter

> “Do you think that, or do you want me to believe you think it?”

This is the line I would test most carefully. It is pointed, but it asks exactly the question Priscilla’s delivery makes relevant.

It also prevents Lavinia from becoming conveniently credulous. She recognizes the possibility of a performance. Priscilla then chooses whether to sustain it.

However, suspicion does not supply certainty. Lavinia can remain unconvinced and still make room beside her.

**Her invitation to sit is permission for that closeness, not an endorsement of the entire account.**

That distinction preserves a future conflict. Priscilla might later overestimate how much her words achieved; Lavinia might discover that she accepted less than Priscilla assumed. Neither outcome is fixed by this passage.

### Priscilla is doing the approaching

She reopens the personal question. She offers an answer. She supplies the disputed admission. She asks for proximity.

Lavinia is not required to pull every expression of desire out of her or threaten departure to get one.

That is the change your critique calls for.

**Priscilla’s vulnerability appears in making an approach whose success she cannot guarantee. Her darker choice appears in what she is willing to misrepresent to improve its chances.**

## 6. Where I would challenge this proposal, too

### Do not make all her kindness counterfeit

If every interest, laugh, and affectionate gesture is only a calculated lure, we have replaced Priscilla with a conventional deceiver who happens to be good at imitation.

That would contradict the genuine care and affection the sources preserve. fileciteturn45file0L2-L2

I would keep the lie specific. She lies about her changed judgment. She need not be lying about wanting the afternoon, enjoying Lavinia’s attention, or finding her attractive.

That specificity makes the betrayal more consequential, not less.

### Do not make Lavinia’s attraction the cause of her own mistreatment

Lavinia’s pleasure and willingness to participate are hers. Priscilla’s deliberate misrepresentation remains Priscilla’s choice.

We should not conclude that Lavinia “asked for it” by wanting someone she distrusts. Equally, we should not erase her active participation and make her nothing but the object of Priscilla’s pursuit.

The fiction can let harmful conduct obtain attention while preserving exactly what happened and what it did not justify. Your authoring agreement explicitly leaves room for that complexity. fileciteturn43file0L114-L120

### The darkness must become readable, not live only in our notes

The passage gives Lavinia reasons to question the admission, but it does not conclusively prove the lie to an audience entering this scene alone.

That can be useful uncertainty. **It cannot become an excuse never to give the audience any basis for distinguishing repentance from performance.**

The complete scene family would need to make Priscilla’s unchanged reasoning perceptible through lawful dialogue or conduct. We should not rely on the hidden Bible, a knowing musical sting, or an explanatory cut into her thoughts.

This is the principal remaining burden of the proposal. I would not call it a finished Dark scene merely because its writer-side motive is suitably disturbing.

## My recommendation

**Rebuild this Dark–Love encounter as active courtship, with a genuine personal disclosure and a deliberately false claim of repentance as the leading candidate.** Keep the repeated departure maneuver out of its center.

Its gain is that the action concerns what Priscilla actually wants: renewed closeness with Lavinia. Its cost is significant: **we would be selecting a new deliberate lie**, not simply intensifying an existing gesture. That needs to remain explicit when comparing or saving the candidate. It is not already established conduct.

And I would keep your central asymmetry: Priscilla is working to draw Lavinia toward her; Lavinia is deciding what she will accept, what she will question, and what she still wants despite the unanswered questions.

Lavinia puts the folded paper back inside the notebook and closes it.

*The excerpt ends during renewed company. Priscilla has obtained private information and a fresh invitation. Lavinia has not forgiven the reading, surrendered the notebook, or agreed that the private instruction represented everything she wanted.*

## 4. Why this has more room for affection and danger

### The pleasure exists before the violation

Priscilla is interested in the imitation, and Lavinia enjoys showing it to her. The long reply gives them something concrete to perform and dispute.

Priscilla can be funny. Lavinia can reject her delivery. Neither needs to be perfectly accurate about the other.

That makes the offered intimacy worthwhile in itself. **The private page is not merely bait we place on the table to make Priscilla behave badly.** Lavinia has a reason to share part of it, and Priscilla has a reason to enjoy the part she was allowed.

The dark choice is the decision that the offered part is not enough.

### Priscilla pursues rather than demanding pursuit

She does not reach for her bag until Lavinia begs her to remain. She does not make Lavinia repeatedly prove that the invitation was sincere.

She says:

> “I’d like to stay.”

That can be completely true.

But she says it after acquiring a piece of Lavinia’s private preparation she was explicitly denied.

**Her desire is not the lie. Her belief that she can use what she has discovered is the danger.**

This follows the character-specific pattern we have already established: understanding something about another person does not grant authority over how that understanding was obtained or used. The Handbook makes her attention both materially effective and capable of becoming invasive. fileciteturn46file0L2-L2

### Lavinia can be affected without being fooled

She sees the turned page. She identifies the intrusion. She asks for the paper back and gets it.

She also hears an offer she may want.

That is the entanglement: **the answer she wanted arrives through a method she did not permit**.

I would not write her as thinking, *It was worth having my privacy invaded because now I know she loves me.* Nor would I force her to end the visit to demonstrate that the intrusion mattered.

Her response can be more particular. She refuses to let the private sentence count as a present invitation, then makes Priscilla ask her directly.

And she says yes.

That yes belongs to the question she has just been asked. It does not reach backward and authorize the reading.

### The cost cannot be completely reversed

Priscilla returns the paper, but she cannot return to not knowing what was on it.

That gives the scene a consequence beyond a momentary argument.

Lavinia now knows that Priscilla crossed a clearly stated limit during an enjoyable encounter. Priscilla now knows something Lavinia had not elected to tell her. They nevertheless continue the visit.

**The closeness does not erase the intrusion, and the intrusion does not make every moment of closeness counterfeit.**

That coexistence is more useful to this Dark–Love candidate than another escalation in which the evening simply becomes intolerable.

## 5. What remains unspoken between them

Notice what they do **not** have to say.

Neither names the earlier institutional document. Neither explains who changed it, why it mattered, or how it affected the company attachment. They already know.

The new action can make that history present through resemblance: Lavinia grants limited access; Priscilla exceeds it; Priscilla then offers something personally meaningful from the knowledge she obtained.

We should allow the audience to notice that pattern without having Lavinia announce, “You have done exactly what you did before.”

Their earlier conflict also remains larger than this new event. Reading a private page and submitting the altered disclosure are different acts with different consequences. One is not a miniature replacement for the other.

The Bible’s clarification remains intact: Priscilla does not morally regret the disclosure intervention. This new scene neither secretly reforms that judgment nor requires her to defend it again. fileciteturn45file0L2-L2

## 6. The challenges I would keep in view

**First, the page must earn its presence.** It extends Lavinia’s established rehearsal habit into a written draft, which is plausible as an invention but not source-established. If the sheet feels planted solely to expose Priscilla’s flaw, the candidate has failed. Their initial enjoyment must be convincing before the reverse side matters.

**Second, “Don’t ask her to stay” cannot be treated as a complete confession.** It might express restraint, anger, embarrassment, an intention to keep the visit short, or conflicting wishes. Priscilla has read a sentence, not obtained access to Lavinia’s entire heart. Her interpretation can still be incomplete.

**Third, the closing request must not turn into a neat lesson.** Lavinia telling Priscilla to ask is not proof that the problem has been repaired. The reader has just seen Priscilla take information she was not offered and then obtain additional company. That is a troubling success even though Lavinia retains control over the immediate invitation.

I would also test whether “That isn’t permission” is too explicit for their voices. Its function is useful, but the wording may be more analytical than the rest of the passage. The refusal to let the page answer for her could instead remain in the combination of taking it back, closing the notebook, and saying, “Then ask me.” I would compare those versions in the assembled scene rather than add more explanation.

## My recommendation

**Keep active courtship and genuine affection, but replace the explicit repentance interview with a present act that exposes Priscilla’s unchanged method.** The private-page version is the leading new candidate I would test, not an approved replacement.

Its gain is that the audience sees the boundary, its crossing, and the personally gratifying result. Its cost is a new private document and a new invasion of privacy. Those are substantive additions, not line edits.

It also gives us more varied dramatic movement without piling on incidents: enjoyment becomes exposure; exposure becomes intrusion; intrusion produces an approach; Lavinia contests its terms and still chooses company.

I like Lavinia humming here because it gives her **an immediate pleasure that does not begin as a performance for Priscilla**.

She can enjoy the phrase, enter where she expects it, and lightly disagree with the recording. Priscilla notices and responds. Neither needs to demonstrate unusual musical expertise.

The brief exchange above suggests that Lavinia knows another version. It does not establish when she heard it, who was with her, or that this is a private song belonging to the relationship.

For this candidate, I prefer that restraint. **The notebook already supplies a clear impression of a shared past. The humming can make the present room feel inhabited.**

We could separately propose a line indicating that Priscilla recognizes Lavinia’s old habit of coming in early. But that would add another piece of prior familiarity. It is available, not necessary.

I would also avoid making the humming stop at the exact instant Lavinia discovers the turned page. That would risk using her voice as a musical warning signal. Let her stop because she speaks, takes a drink, or turns her attention to something else.

And I would not connect the tune, the old memo, the England entries, and the forbidden page into one hidden solution. **They can occupy the same life without all being parts of the same clue.**

## 6. What I love most about them as characters

**They can be remarkably attentive to each other and still disagree about what that attention permits.**

Priscilla may remember a tiny preference, recognize a sentence, or understand why Lavinia found something funny. Those moments can make her company genuinely desirable. Yet she can turn that same accuracy into a reason to proceed past a limit she was given.

Lavinia can appreciate the attention and remain angry. She can keep an affectionate note without approving its author’s later conduct. She can offer a piece of her private imagination because she wants Priscilla to enjoy it, while still having other pages she wants kept to herself.

That combination gives the notebook emotional weight. **It is not embarrassing merely because it contains evidence of love. It matters because it belongs to a private life Lavinia is entitled to share selectively.**

I also love that their pleasures need not be grand. A ridiculous imitation, a remembered disagreement about a book, a dance with an imperfect first step, or a preference about tea can make their company worth wanting.

Those moments do not certify that the relationship is safe. They explain why its losses and violations matter.

And for the darker scene, the most compelling Priscilla is not someone who feels nothing while calculating everything. **She can be sincerely touched that Lavinia kept her note, then make a deliberate, invasive choice because she wants more of that knowledge.** Her affection does not disappear at the boundary. It fails to stop her crossing it.

That is the version I would explore, while preserving your clarification that tenderness or acknowledgment of hurt does not become repentance for the disclosure amendment. fileciteturn45file0L2-L2

**My recommendation is a notebook containing a few treasures, selected recollections, and clearly distinguishable rehearsals; humming as ordinary enjoyment; and a deliberate intrusion whose consequences cannot be erased by the affection surrounding it.**
